newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Iraqi envoy to see U.N.'s oil-for-food" official.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi envoy to see U.N.'s oil-for-food" official.

text.p: Iraqi U.N. ambassador Nizar Hamdoon was scheduled to confer Monday with U.N. Under Secretary-General Chinmaya Gharekhan, the U.N. official who oversees the proposed Iraqi "oil-for-food" deal, an Iraqi source said.
There was no immediate word about the subject of the meeting, which is set for 1000 EST/1500 GMT.
The "oil-for-food" deal, signed in May and permitting Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil to buy food, medicine and other humanitarian supplies, has been on hold for months.
Although ready to go into force in September, it was delayed after Iraq sent its troops into the north of the country in late August to back one side in an inter-Kurdish conflict.
The United Nations said at the time security conditions in the region did not permit the deployment of U.N. staff to monitor the deal.
The United Nations and Iraq have also been at odds over demands by Baghdad to control the number and make-up of the U.N. monitoring team.
Iraq last week submitted to the United Nations its latest oil-pricing formula, for December, that would govern oil contracts once the scheme gets underway.

It has yet to be approved by the Security Council's Iraqi sanctions committee, where the United States has blocked previous months' formulas submitted by Iraq on grounds they are irrelevant until the problems relating to U.N. monitors have been settled.
